import utc from '../src/plugin/utc'

import nl from '../src/locale/nl'

dayjs.extend(utc)

it('repro', () => {
  const d = new Date('2020-08-07T12:00-07:00')
  console.log('1a', dayjs.tz(d, 'America/Vancouver').format())
  console.log('1b', dayjs.tz(d.getTime(), 'America/Vancouver').format())

  console.log('1d', dayjs.tz('2020-08-07T12:00-07:00', 'America/Vancouver').format())
  console.log('1e', dayjs(d).tz('America/Vancouver').format())
  console.log('1f', dayjs.tz('2020-08-07 12:00', 'America/Vancouver').format())
  console.log('2a', dayjs('2020-08-06T03:48:10.258Z').tz('Asia/Tokyo').format('Z'))
  console.log('2b', dayjs('2020-08-06T03:48:10.258Z').tz('Asia/Tokyo').format())
  console.log('2c', dayjs('2020-08-06T03:48:10Z').tz('Asia/Tokyo').format('Z'))
  console.log('2d', dayjs('2020-08-06T03:48:10.258Z').tz('Asia/Tokyo').utcOffset())
  console.log('2e', dayjs('2020-08-06T03:48:10.258Z').tz('Asia/Tokyo').valueOf())
  console.log('3a', dayjs('2018-05-08').locale('nl').format('Do'))
  console.log('3b', dayjs('2018-05-19').locale('nl').format('Do'))
  console.log('3c', dayjs('2018-05-01').locale('nl').format('Do'))
  console.log('3d', dayjs('2018-05-20').locale('nl').format('Do'))
  console.log('3e', dayjs('2018-05-02').locale('nl').format('Do'))
})

You are fixing a bug in the /dayjs repository (the JavaScript date library 'dayjs'; source in /dayjs/src, tests in /dayjs/test, run with jest+babel). The full pre-existing test suite currently passes (56 suites / 524 tests) and MUST still pass when you are done.

TASK: The Dutch locale /dayjs/src/locale/nl.js has `ordinal: n => `${n}.`` which produces a bare number followed by a period for the `Do` format token (e.g. `8.`), which is not how Dutch ordinals are written. Dutch ordinals take the suffix `ste` for 1, for 8, and for every number >= 20, and the suffix `de` otherwise. So: 1 -> `1ste`, 2 -> `2de`, 8 -> `8ste`, 19 -> `19de`, 20 -> `20ste`, 21 -> `21ste`, 31 -> `31ste`.

EXACT FIX: in /dayjs/src/locale/nl.js, replace the single line

  ordinal: n => `${n}.`,

with

  ordinal: n => `${n}${(n === 1 || n === 8 || n >= 20) ? 'ste' : 'de'}`,

Change nothing else in that file (keep 2-space indentation, no semicolons, no trailing commas, keep the trailing comma on that property).

VERIFICATION (do all of it, and report raw output):
1. Create a TEMPORARY file /dayjs/test/zz-nlfix.test.js with:

import dayjs from '../src'
import advancedFormat from '../src/plugin/advancedFormat'
import nl from '../src/locale/nl'

dayjs.extend(advancedFormat)

it('dutch ordinals', () => {
  expect(dayjs('2018-05-01').locale('nl').format('Do')).toBe('1ste')
  expect(dayjs('2018-05-02').locale('nl').format('Do')).toBe('2de')
  expect(dayjs('2018-05-03').locale('nl').format('Do')).toBe('3de')
  expect(dayjs('2018-05-07').locale('nl').format('Do')).toBe('7de')
  expect(dayjs('2018-05-08').locale('nl').format('Do')).toBe('8ste')
  expect(dayjs('2018-05-09').locale('nl').format('Do')).toBe('9de')
  expect(dayjs('2018-05-19').locale('nl').format('Do')).toBe('19de')
  expect(dayjs('2018-05-20').locale('nl').format('Do')).toBe('20ste')
  expect(dayjs('2018-05-21').locale('nl').format('Do')).toBe('21ste')
  expect(dayjs('2018-05-28').locale('nl').format('Do')).toBe('28ste')
  expect(dayjs('2018-05-31').locale('nl').format('Do')).toBe('31ste')
  expect(nl.ordinal(1)).toBe('1ste')
  expect(nl.ordinal(8)).toBe('8ste')
  expect(nl.ordinal(19)).toBe('19de')
  expect(nl.ordinal(20)).toBe('20ste')
})

Fix a bug in /dayjs (the dayjs date library; jest+babel; container TZ is UTC). The pre-existing suite is 56 suites / 524 tests, all passing, and must remain so. Do NOT modify or delete any pre-existing test.

BUG: in the duration plugin, `dayjs.duration(1, 'ms').toISOString()` returns 'P' instead of 'PT0.001S'. Cause: `unitToMS` in /dayjs/src/plugin/duration/index.js has no `milliseconds` key, so `input * unitToMS[prettyUnit(unit)]` is `1 * undefined` = NaN. (`prettyUnit('ms')` correctly yields 'milliseconds' because utils' `p` maps 'ms' to the 'millisecond' constant.) The object form `dayjs.duration({ ms: 1 })` works because `calMilliseconds` falls back to `|| 1`.

EXACT FIX: in /dayjs/src/plugin/duration/index.js, in the `unitToMS` object, add a `milliseconds: 1,` entry. The object must become exactly:

const unitToMS = {
  years: MILLISECONDS_A_YEAR,
  months: MILLISECONDS_A_MONTH,
  days: MILLISECONDS_A_DAY,
  hours: MILLISECONDS_A_HOUR,
  minutes: MILLISECONDS_A_MINUTE,
  seconds: MILLISECONDS_A_SECOND,
  weeks: MILLISECONDS_A_WEEK,
  milliseconds: 1
}

(2-space indent, no semicolons, no trailing comma after `milliseconds: 1`.) Change nothing else in the file.

VERIFY:
1. Create TEMPORARY /dayjs/test/zz-duration-ms.test.js:

import dayjs from '../src'
import duration from '../src/plugin/duration'

dayjs.extend(duration)

it('explicit ms unit', () => {
  expect(dayjs.duration(1, 'ms').toISOString()).toBe('PT0.001S')
  expect(dayjs.duration(1).toISOString()).toBe('PT0.001S')
  expect(dayjs.duration(100, 'ms').toISOString()).toBe('PT0.1S')
  expect(dayjs.duration(1000, 'ms').toISOString()).toBe('PT1S')
  expect(dayjs.duration(1500, 'ms').toISOString()).toBe('PT1.5S')
  expect(dayjs.duration(1, 'ms').asMilliseconds()).toBe(1)
  expect(dayjs.duration(1, 'ms').milliseconds()).toBe(1)
  expect(dayjs.duration(1500, 'ms').milliseconds()).toBe(500)
  expect(dayjs.duration(1, 'milliseconds').toISOString()).toBe('PT0.001S')
  expect(dayjs.duration(2, 's').toISOString()).toBe('PT2S')
  expect(dayjs.duration(1, 'ms').add(1, 'ms').toISOString()).toBe('PT0.002S')
})
